articleTitle: Gyrotron development activity at varian associates
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Recent progress on a number of gyrotron development projects at Varian Associates will be summarized. On one project pulsed output of 100 kW has been obtained at 140 GHz with TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</inf> mode output. The same device has produced 100 kW at 160 GHz with the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">62</inf> mode. Recent experience operating 200 kW oscillators at 60 and 70 GHz with pulse lengths of several seconds will be discussed. This long pulse operation requires heater compensation to maintain constant beam current from the temperature limited cathodes. Recent computer simulations of gyrotron guns will be presented. These exhibit some interesting space charge effects which become particularly important in megawatt level beams.

articleTitle: New possibilities of linear pyroelectric arrays for infrared detection and imaging
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The peculiar surface properties of ferroelectric crystals (1) (2) are attractive to use in pyroelectric detection. It will be shown that extremely cheap linear pyroelectric arrays of detectors are feasible with up to 1 000 elements (each one 20 μm × 20 μm) and a reasonable NEP ≅ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−11</sup> watts. This allows several applications where both room temperature and low cost of operation are needed (i.e. Remote Ground Sensors; Unattended Ground Sensors, Line/For Missiles…).

articleTitle: Backward-wave oscillators for frequencies above 600 GHz
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: New concepts are being investigated for making BWO's for frequencies above 600 GHz and up to at least 2,000 GHz. Ion beam assisted etching is being used to make small slow-wave circuits on diamond. An experiment with an 18 μm pitch inter-digital line etched on diamond, designed to oscillate at 600 GHz with a 4 kV beam and 3 kG magnetic field, is being constructed.

articleTitle: The dielectric resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: There is, today, strong interest on the part of both military and commercial users, in antenna systems which can operate efficiently in the millimeter wave region (100–300 GHz) and above. Reducing the size of currently-used microwave frequency antennas to obtain higher resonant frequencies will usually be unsuccessful, either because the small size prohibits economical fabrication or because the inherently larger conduction losses at the higher frequencies result in inefficient operation.

articleTitle: Survey of millimeter wave antennas
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An overview over the area of mm-wave antennas is presented. For the purpose of the review, mm-wave radiating structures are grouped into two classes, i.e., antennas of conventional configuration and antennas based on new design concepts.

articleTitle: MM-wave IMPATT diodes with integrated gold straps
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Impatt diodes as well as other semiconductor devices demand increasing efforts in packaging technique and reducing of parasitic impedance with increasing frequency, because the dimensions of the device itself decrease rapidly. Even with devices with nearly the same dimensions and cw-characteristics it is not possible to reach reproducible RF-conditions with the existing packaging technique /1/.

articleTitle: W-band beam lead planar doped barrier subharmonic mixer
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Beam lead GaAs planar doped barrier (PDB) devices have been developed for use as subharmonically pumped mixers at millimeter wave frequencies. This paper will cover details of device fabrication, and give experimental results of the subharmonic mixer performance in W-band (75.00 – 110.00 GHz).

articleTitle: Diagnostic applications of millimeter waves in coal conversion systems
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The feasibility of millimeter-wave (MMW) techniques is discussed for in-situ diagnostics of particulate-laden multiphase streams in coal conversion and combustion systems. The techniques investigated include MMW spectroscopy for determination of molecular species and gas-phase temperature, MMW radiometry for particle temperature measurement, and MMW scattering for particle characterization. The theoretical feasibility of each technique is presented together with the applicable range of measurement/system parameters.

articleTitle: Comparative studies of Si, GaAs and InP millimeter-wave impatt diodes
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: With the increasing interest in millimeter-wave applications, there is a renewed demand for solid state sources with ever higher output power levels and efficiencies. At present, high efficiency oscillators above 100 GHz have been fabricated from silicon diodes. However, recent progress in GaAs and InP technology [1] [3] raise the possibility to use these materials. In this context, it appears necessary to investigate from a theoretical point of view their respective capabilities. The purpose of this paper is to present results of simulation of Si, GaAs and InP double drift region diodes in the 94, 140 and 220 atmospheric attenuation windows.

articleTitle: Recent developments in millimeter wave planar filters and diplexers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper describes the performance of recently developed millimeter wave planar filters and diplexers using microstrip, suspended stripline, and finline techniques. State-of-the-art performances for these components have been obtained and have played important roles in the successful developments of various millimeter-wave components and systems.

articleTitle: Study of saturation effect and output power of optically pumped FIR lasers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In this paper, the saturation effect, output power and the optimum operating pressure of optically pumped FIR lasers were studied theoretically. The density matrix equation of six-level system has been solved, in case the FIR wave signals in the system were not small enough to be neglected.

articleTitle: Field enhancement and increased island array selectivity of the discontinuous MIM film diode
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The receiving properties of the discontinuous metal-Insulator-metal film diode are significantly Improved by the Incorporation of the tungsten whisker antenna that enhances the Incident field strength over selected metal Island arrays for optimum conduction paths. The planar version Is also mechanically stable.

articleTitle: Observation of collective thomson scattering of D2O laser radiation from a tokamak plasma
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Collective Thomson Scattering from thermal density fluctuations using a pulsed, high power far-infrared laser offers several advantages as a means to measure the ion temperature in a tokamak plasma /1/. In order to demonstrate the feasibility of such a measurement, an experiment has been set up at the TCA Tokamak of the CRPP. A similar study has been carried out before by Woskoboinikow et al. on Alcator C of the M.I.T., Cambridge, Massachusetts /2/.

articleTitle: Diode-laser infrared heterodyne radiometer at 28 μm
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An infrared heterodyne radiometer has been constructed which operates at 28 μm with a PbSnSe diode laser local oscillator and a HgCdTe photodiode photomixer, both cooled to about 20 K. In spite of low power and excess noise of the diode laser and weak rectification characteristics of the photodiode, a heterodyne NEP of 3.5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−19</sup> W/Hz was measured over a bandwidth of 500 MHz.

articleTitle: Use of the geometrical theory of diffraction in the design of millimetre and submillimetre-wave systems
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (GTD) has been widely used in the design of microwave antennas but has been little used in the design of near- and sub-millimetre-wave systems. It is particularly useful in situations where large-angle near-field diffraction effects are important. The application of GTD in the design of a near-millimetre-wave radiometer will be described here to illustrate the method.

articleTitle: Observations on a powerful and stable CH3OH laser
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Diagnostics for high density plasma generated in Tokamak devices requires laser sources with suitable wavelenght and power.

articleTitle: Prospects for high frequency, megawatt gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An overview of recent experimental and theoretical progess at MIT on the development of high frequency (>100 GHz) gyrotrons will be given. A parametric analysis has been completed that indicates that cw gyrotrons operating at these frequencies are capable of powers in excess of 1 MW with high efficiency. The design parameters of 1 and 10 MW, 120 GHz monotrons will be reviewed. A 1 MW, 120–140 GHz pulsed gyrotron is presently being constructed at MIT and should be operational by early 1986.

articleTitle: A new kind of special axisymmetric quasi-optical resonance system with three mirrors
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Recently, the open cavity has been widely used in millimeter devices even including the gyrotron. Usually the Fabry-Perot type of open cavity is used, but as it is noted in [1][7–9], that the Fabry-Perot open cavity is far from the ideal resonance system for gyrotron structure, because it is difficult to fit the magnetron-injection gun, which is successfully used in gyrotron for many years.

articleTitle: Niobium nitride devices for SIS mixers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The superconductor-insulator-superconductor (SIS) tunnel junction is an attractive candidate for millimeter wave mixers offering conversion gain and quantum limited noise.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> SIS mixers have been operated at 36 GHz with a single sideband noise temperature of 3.7K which is within a factor of 2 of quantum limited performance.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> These results were obtained with devices fabricated from lead alloy technology. While this technology is very useful for the demonstration of quantum limited noise an all refractory junction technology would be desirable as it would have the advantages of being mechanically rugged, cycle well between room temperature and 4K be resistant to radiation damage and have enhanced high frequency response.

articleTitle: Suppression of axial mode competition in a high-harmonic gyromonotron
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The high-harmonic gyromonotron is based on the synchronous interaction between axis-encircling electrons and a high-order azimuthal TE cylindrical cavity mode. Harmonic operation together with RF acceleration of the electron beam constitute a compact moderate- to high-power millimeter wave source. Axial mode competition, a serious problem for high-harmonic operation, has been suppressed by inserting a thin, lossy dielectric ring along the cavity midplane. The cavity was observed to operate at the fourth harmonic without mode competition, emitting monochromatic 32 GHz radiation with 16% efficiency.

articleTitle: Scattering from ECRF waves
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: There has heen considerable progress made in the heating of tokamak and mirror plasmas in the electron cyclotron range of frequencies (ECRF) due to the recent availability of high power millimeter wave gyrotrons. Both O-mode and X-mode heating studies have been performed using, outside and inside wave launching structures.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1,2)</sup> In Doublet-III, electron temperatures have increased from ≃ 1 keV to > 2 keV using 750 kW of 60 GHz heating power. Furthermore, in PDX electron temperature increases from ≃ 1.5keV to ≃ 3keV have been observed in the central plasma region with ≃ 80kW input power at 60 GHz. In addition, several interesting observations have also been made. First, the 60 GHz radiation that was transmitted through the plasma into the low field region was spectrally resolved. Satellites separated by the lower hybrid frequency were observed indicative of parametric decay. Second, the heating power was deposited locally and was therefore large compared to the ohmic heating power in the central region. This therefore resulted in steep temperature gradients over distances of only ≃ 10–15cm which can strongly affect the low frequency microturbulence.

articleTitle: Results from the NRL ubitron experiment
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An experimental program to study the potential of the ubitron interaction mechanism is underway at the Naval Research Laboratory. The ubitron, a device based on a fast-wave, periodic-beam interaction, was developed by R. M. Phillips in the late 1950's [1]. Although Phillips obtained impressive results In several amplifier experiments, research on the ubitron was stopped in 1964. Recent theoretical and experimental advances in a related area, free-electron lasers, suggest that ubitron performance has been underestimated. Key developments for improved performance include the use of circularly polarized magnetic wiggler and waveguide fields, high quality electron beams, gyroresonant enhancement of the magnetic wiggler, and enhancement through system parameter tapering. An amplifier experiment has been constructed at NRL to explore the effects of these developments on the gain and efficiency limits of the ubitron.

articleTitle: Domino-type millimeter-wave systems
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A new concept for assembling millimeter-wave systems without use of connectors and flanges is described.

articleTitle: A 120 GHz, TE03 mode gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A high-frequency gyrotron (120 GHz, TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</inf> mode) was designed and is being constructed at Mitsubishi Electric Corporation. Output power of about 30 kW is expected at the beam voltage of 30 kV and the beam current of 3 A.

articleTitle: Atmospheric refraction and absorption and their fluctuations at centimeter and millimeter waves
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Four topics are discussed here. First, the near-line-center absorption line shape of water vapor is shown to be the Van Vleck-Weisskopf shape. Second, Gordon's theory is recommended for calculation of absorption by the tails of the 60 GHz band of oxygen and the oxygen nonresonant absorption. Third, the dispersive refractivity from water-vapor lines above 1 THz is reduced to a simple calculation. Fourth, a model of refraction and absorption and their sensitivity to fluctuations of temperature and humidity is described.

articleTitle: Advanced gyroklystron at NRL
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The Naval Research Laboratory (NRL) has successfully demonstrated that gyroklystrons can be operated stably at high efficiency. The recent experiments with the three cavity, fundamental mode GKLY-101 gyroklystron showed 30% efficient, stable operation at 4.5 GHz with peak powers on the order of 50kW. In order to obtain high powers at mm-wavelengths it will be necessary to operate at least the last cavity of the gyroklystron as an overmoded cavity. To examine the feasibility of such a device NRL is building a second generation tube, GKLY-201, which will be a four cavity device operating the last cavity in the circular TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">131</inf> mode. The first three cavities will operate in the rectangular TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">101</inf> mode and will act to stablize the gyroklystron operation in the last cavity. Anticipated output power is 200kW for 3<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μs</inf> pulses at a frequency of 4.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave propagation in arid land — A field study in Riyadh
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A field study is presently underway in Riyadh to study the effects of main, sand storms and multlpath fading on millimetric wave propagation. The study involves computerized monitoring of five radio links and a meteorological station. The paper described the experiment and reports results to date.

articleTitle: Analysis of a high harmonic rectangular gyrotron using ribbon beams
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Results of the theoretical analysis of a high harmonic axially grooved rectangular gyrotron using a ribbon beam are discussed. Optimization of the operating parameters of the gyrotron is made for maximum efficiency of conversion through the solution of the linearized relativistic Vlasov equation and non-linear particle simulations. Results for a gyrotron using a ribbon beam simulated by 1200 electrons and operating at 90 GHz and the 6th harmonic are presented.

articleTitle: Microstrip fully integrated W-band transceiver using soft substrate
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper describes the performance of various W-band (75–110 GHz) microstrip components including Gunn LOs, mixers and couplers, etc. on soft substrate. Using these components a integrated transceiver was developed. Results show a power output of 3.0 mW at 90.0 GHz with Δ F = ± 150 MHz and noise figure (DSB) ≤ 12.0db. Experiment and theory are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Far infrared studies of lattice and free carrier effects in narrow-gap semiconductors
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Far infrared (FIR) studies in narrow-gap semiconductors have attracted considerable attention because of providing information about both lattice and free carrier. Recent work of FIR reflection measurement in narrow-gap semiconductor Cd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Hg<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Se showed the importance of the contribution of interband term in dielectric function and the plasmon-LO phonon coupling [1]. Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Hg<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Se (ZnHgSe) crystals are mixed-compounds of zero-gap semiconductor HgSe and wide-gap semiconductor ZnSe. This mixed compounds crystallize in zincblende structure in the whole range of mole fraction x. The energy gap and the symmetry of the conduction band of the crystals depend on x. The experiments of Schubnikov de Haas effect in ZnHgSe with small x showed the strong nonlinear dependence of the energy gap on composition and the semimetal-semiconductor transition (x = 0.03) at 4 K[2]. Carrier scattering mechanisms were also reported in this material[3]. Nevertheless, little is known about the FIR studies in this material. In this note, we analyze the reflection spectra in ZnHgSe.

articleTitle: Matched loads for high-power gyrotron tests
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Different matched loads for gyrotron tests were developed and built: 1) Loads with a solid state absorber (fire clay) were made for tests of 70 GHz gyrotrons. These loads dissipated 200 kW/100 ms pulses at full gyrotron duty cycle with negligible reflections. Two types of these loads were produced, one for the axisymmetric TEon modes and another for the linearly polarized TE11 and HE11 modes. 2) Calorimeter loads were manufactured for calibrated power measurements, containing an absorbing and cooling fluid with significantly larger attenuation length than water. This allows a drastic reduction of the flow rate without any boiling or blistering even at longer pulses (≈ 100 ms). Another advantage is a much higher precision of the calibration procedure.

articleTitle: 90/180 GHz millimeter wave radiometer for future airborne measurements
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A 90/180 GHz multichannel radiometer was developed using a common lens antenna and dual corrugated feedhorns. The radiometer was designed to mount in a modified window port on NASA's Convair 990 (CV-990) aircraft. The operating bandwidths of the instrument's three IF channels coincide with the proposed AMSU sensor scheduled for future space borne measurements.

articleTitle: A simple self-consistent analysis of the gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A non-linear, multi-mode, time-domain analysis of the gyrotron is proposed. The e.m. fields are expanded into empty cavity modes, yielding a set of ordinary differential equations for the time-dependent expansion coefficients. These equations are coupled to the equations of electron motion. — Transient and steady-state characteristics are thus calculated.

articleTitle: Optimized overmoded TE01-TO-TM11 mode converters for high-power millimeter wave applications at 70 and 110 GHZ
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Mode coupling in bent, oversized, smooth-walled circular waveguides was studied by means of numerical integration of coupled-mode equations in order to optimize high-power TE01-to-TM11 mode transducers at 70 and 110 GHz. Such transducers are used in the mode conversion sequence TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf> to TE01 to TM11 to HE11 for generating the linearly polarized HE11 (Gaussian like) mode from circular electric TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf> gyrotron modes. The balanced HE11 hybrid mode is in many respects ideal for electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) of plasmas in thermonuclear fusion research, or for other technical applications. The lowest level of unwanted spurious modes is achieved with sinusoidal curvature distribution instead of constant curvature. The calculated efficiencies of 97.9 % at 70 GHz and 95.2 % at 140 GHz (I.D. = 27.8 mm, ohmic attenuation is included) are in excellent agreement with the measured ones (97.6±0.1)% and (95±1)%, respectively.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental investigation of phase fluctuations in an absorption region
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The differential phase scintillations between two neighbouring frequencies on the side of the oxygen absorption peak have been measured. The −8/3 slope of the asymptotes to the measured spectra at the lowest and highest scintillation frequencies and the spectral ratio between these asymptotes are in good agreement with the theoretical predictions presented.

articleTitle: Self consistent approaches for the gyroklystron and the gyrotwystron
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In the first calculation, the optimization of gyroklystron efficiency is investigated by employing a two-step procedure. As a first step, the prebuncher is analyzed using a small signal approximation, since the cavity(ies) here serve mainly to modulate slightly the velocities of the electrons, which will be bunched in the field-free drift section(s). It is found that the electrons entering the energy extraction cavity can be characterized entirely by only two dimensionless parameters: a bunching parameter q and a relative phase ψ. The numerical simulation of the extraction cavity, based on the nonlinear pendulum equations describing the interaction between the electrons and the rf field, supplemented by the initial conditions specified by q and ψ, constitutes the second step. The final result of this two-step analysis is the efficiency, η<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥opt</inf> optimized with respect to q ψ and the magnetic detuning parameter Δ. This efficiency depends only on the normalized cavity length μ and the normalized rf field F of the energy extraction section. The efficiency as well as the conditions required to attain this optimum (q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">op</inf>, Δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">opt</inf>, and ψ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">opt</inf>) are presented as contour plots on the (F, μ) plane and can be used efficiently to design gyroklystons of any frequency and output power.

articleTitle: Properties of infrared thin-film antennas at 10.6μm
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Antenna coupled point-contact devices, such as MOM diodes[1,2], Schottky diodes[3] and warm(hot) carrier devices[4] are well known as detectors and mixers for wavelengths less than 1mm, and a tungsten cat-whiskers mechanically contacted to the diodes works as antennas quite well. However, these cat-whisker antennas tend to be mechanically franqible and unstable. Furthermore, a stable and reproducible antenna configuration is difficult to realize using the thin, free standing whiskers.

articleTitle: The analytic nonlinear investigation of electron cyclotron maser
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In the low voltage range, the linear growing rate Β and the maximum field amplitude Rm increase when U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> becomes higher. On the other hand, u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>/µ is small and the electrons can locate in the favourable phase where the electrons deliver energy to the field. Thus, the efficiency increases as U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> rises. In this case, the amount of the field energy extracted from the beam mainly depends on the energy which can be delivered out by the beam and was called as "free energy"<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(2)</sup>.

articleTitle: Optically controlled coplanar waveguide millimeter wave phase shifter
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A new optically controlled millimeter wave phase shifter is discussed. The device is based on the interaction between the guided wave on a coplanar waveguide (CPW) and an optically induced electron-hole plasma in the CPW semiconductor substrate. A prototype structure consisting of a Schottky-contacted coplanar waveguide on a multilayer AlGaAs/GaAs substrate is modeled. Optically-induced electron-hole plasma densities are calculated using the nonlinear diffusion equation, valid for high level injection in semiconductors. Numerical calculations of the phase shift and insertion loss versus illumination intensity are found based on these plasma densities.

articleTitle: Microwave resonance of a large electron-hole drop in strained Germanium
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: By means of 35 GHz circular-polarizing waveguide system, Alfvén wave dimensional resonance of a large drop in strained Ge is observed separately for the electron-active and for the hole-active modes. Resonance behavior shows difference between each mode in some respects. From magnetic field position of the resonance, radial decay of a large drop is derived. Carrier scattering rate in a large drop is also discussed from resonance line-width.

articleTitle: An improved design for TE02-TE01 and TE01-TE11 mode converters for use with mm-wave gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An improved design is discussed for a varying-radius type TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf>-to-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode converter and a TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>-to-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> serpentine mode converter for a 1.094“ diameter circular waveguide at 60 GHz. This design gives shorter converter lengths for the same or higher converter efficiencies than previous designs as well as broader bandwidths.

articleTitle: 10-channel grating polychromator for electron cyclotron emission measurement in JIPP T-II U tokamak
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The measurements of electron cyclotron emission (ECE) is very important for the diagnostics of high-temperature tokamak plasma. As an instrument for the measurements, we have constructed a 10-channel grating polychromator having high temporal and spatial resolution [1]. We have applied it for the measurements of ECE from JIPP T-II U. The spectrometer and the experimental results will be shown.

articleTitle: SMMW detectors; quasiparticle mixer and Josephson mixer using superconducting tunnel junction
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: There are growing needs for low noise and wide band receiver in SMMW range, e.g., in radio astronomy [1]. Hitherto, Schottky diode mixer, Josephson mixer using point contact microbridges, and quasiparticle mixer using superconducting tunnel junctions have been investigated intensively in MMW range. Over wide SMMW range, however, only Schottky diode mixer was tested and used at present. Quasiparticle mixer now confronts a basic difficulty for operation in SMMW range, although it has very high potential as a SMMW mixer. On the otherhand, potential of Josephson mixer using microbridges is unclear.

articleTitle: Comparative study of millimeter-wave guiding structures
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A number of guided wave structures for millimeter-wave circuits are compared in terms of the characteristics and applications.

articleTitle: The transmission behaviour of the H waveguide. application to the design of a broadband launcher
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In recent developments the transmission lines used for millimeter-waves propagation are, usually, non shielded dielectric waveguides which present parasitic radiation in the discontinuities. Nevertheless, long time ago, the H-waveguide was proposed (1) for this purpose, because of its decreasing conductor losses with increasing frequency. On the other hand, some works ((2) and (3)) aiming to the design of isolators and differential phase-shifters show that multi-H waveguide is a good transmission line for this purpose. But, age neralized use of a type of transmission line needs of a complete knowledge of the propagation behaviour (guided wavelength, conductor and dielectric losses and characteristic impedance). This paper presents some computed results for these performances and the application to the design of a broadband launcher from standard rectangular waveguides to these ones.

articleTitle: On the kinetic theory of electron cyclotron maser
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper starts from the kinetic theory to expound the method of characteristics. Influence of the equilibrium distribution f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> upon analyzed result is fully investigated. Dispersion equation is rigorously derived in waveguide coordinate system in case of interaction between TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mn</inf> field in a circular waveguide and a single momentum ring-shaped electron beam.

articleTitle: Scattering from a periodic array of apertures or plates where the conductors have arbitrary shape, thickness, and resistivity
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The current distribution and reflection coefficients for a periodic array of arbitrary shaped conductors illuminated by a plane wave is obtained through a rooftop current approximation. Results are given and compared with the literature.

articleTitle: MM-wave dielectric ring resonators
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Ring resonators fabricated by filling a rectangular cross-section groove in a polypropylene substrate with a dielectric powder exhibit Q's as high as 2400 at 94 GHz in an 8 cm diameter ring. Directional coupling from adjacent straight dielectric guides was used to form a transmission filter. Previously, we demonstrated a mm-wave dielectric channel waveguide with .09 dB/cm loss (Refs. 1,2) consisting of a rectangular groove in the surface of a plastic substrate filled with a low-loss, high dielectric constant powder. Here we describe mm-wave ring resonators made from powder-core dielectric channel waveguide.

articleTitle: Transmission and tunability of a double-disc gyrotron window at 120 – 160 GHz
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The power reflection coefficient |ρ|<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of a double-disc gyrotron window is examined in the frequency range 120 – 160 GHz emphasizing tolerances in the dielectric constants of the discs and the influence of disc separation. The waveguide diameter is 70 mm and the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>, TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</inf> and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">06</inf> modes are considered. The double-disc window can be made reflectionless at a given frequency by changing the disc separation. This allows for compensation of variable dielectric constants and for tuning to the produced waveguide mode. Experimental results are given for 116–151 GHz.

articleTitle: The application of homodyne spectroscopy to the study of low frequency microturbulence in the text tokamak
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The propagation direction of tokamak density fluctuations is typically determined by employing heterodyne detection techniques. Such methods require two coherent sources employed as the incident and local oscillator beams. Realization of such a system in the far-infrared is expensive and technically nontrivial. Utilization of a rotating grating to frequency shift a portion of the source beam is a feasible alternative although the frequency offset is limited to roughly Δ v ≤ 150 kHz (insufficient for microturbulence measurements where fluctuations are observed up to 1 MHz).

articleTitle: Front-end components for submillimeter-wave Schottky-diode receivers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Two key components of a submillimeter-wave (SW) heterodyne receiver for 890 GHz operation are described. The quasi-optical diplexer uses parallel metallic-wire grids as semi-transparent elements to combine both the local oscillator (LO) and signal radiations. It exhibits less than 1 dB insertion loss in the signal path and over 30 dB rejection ratio in the L0 path. The mixer block uses an original combination of plane reflectors to increase the electromagnetic coupling factor between the SW beam and the antenna connected to the mixing Schottky diode. An improvement of 7–8 dB with respect to a totally open structure has been obtained.

articleTitle: Analysis of azimuthally magnetized solid-plasma circular guide
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An analysis is presented of a circular guide containing azimuthally magnetized solid-plasma using InSb at 77 K as plasma material. The potentialities of the gyrotropic guide in designing practical nonreciprocal magnetoplasma devices for millimeter waves are discussed.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave attenuation measurements in layer structured semiconductor waveguides
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Using an optoelectronic technique, we have measured the attenuation of millimeter-waves propagating in Si, SOS, and GaAs/AlGaAs/GaAs epilayer waveguides illuminated by 1,060 nm and 532 nm wavelength laser pulses. A comparison with theoretical calculations and a discussion of design criteria to obtain a pure phase shifter are given.

articleTitle: Concept of infrared laser particle accelerators with oversized DBR and HFB waveguides
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We present an infrared laser accelerator concept which makes use of hollow oversized periodic or helical waveguide structures originally designed for distributed (DFB) and helical (HFB) feedback lasers. Fields and advantages relative to other laser-accelerator schemes are discussed.

articleTitle: Small period electromagnet higglers for free electron lasers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Small period wiggler magnets for Free Electron Lasers (FEL's) are currently a topic of considerable interest because a small wiggler period leads to a reduced electron energy requirement for a desired radiation wavelength. A great deal of effort has been expended on the design of permanent magnet wigglers in recent years,<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> and high quality wigglers of this type have been constructed with periods typically in the range 1–10 cm (although methods for constructing even shorter period wigglers are currently under development). Recently our group has reported<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> a technique for fabricating small period (1–10 mm) electromagnetic wigglers in which the magnetic field amplitude can be varied continuously by varying the current in the electromagnet “windings.” In addition, the proposed design is bilateral, thus increasing the magnetic field amplitude and reducing the transverse gradient in the magnetic field in the central region betwen the two magnetic structures. As these wiggler electromagnets are inexpensive and easily constructed, they might prove useful for studying FEL physics and for the development of practical, lower voltage, FEL devices. In this paper we present the initial results from a program to investigate the performance characteristics of such wiggler electromagnets, and gain and efficiency calculations for an FEL employing a small period electromagnet wiggler of this type.

articleTitle: Analysis of the propagation properties including the single-mode bandwidth in an insular dielectric waveguide
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In this paper the conditions is derived which six lower modes satisfied respectively in an insular dielectric waveguide. The method of optimal design is also dealt with for five parameters selected by the improved Orthogonal Array Table (OAT), which affect the propagation propeties including the single-mode bandwidth. A set of parameters is presented, by which the insular dielectric waveguide has optimal propagation properties. It is not significant that the single-mode bandwidth in an image waveguide is compared with that in an insular dielectric waveguide, because the lowest mode E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> in an image waveguide is one without cut-off.

articleTitle: ECH gyrotron system for the tara tandem mirror
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Tailoring the hot electron energy distribution provides a means of manipulating the electrostatic potential in the plasma which can in turn provide electrostatic plasma confinement. Production of a hot electron population is a result of electron cyclotron heating at the fundamental and second harmonic provided by pulsed 28 GHz gyrotons (75 ms, 200 kW). Corrugated bends with carborundum sections reduce the nonsymmetric mode content. Both focused and unfocused Vlasov antennas are used to launch the rf power. Water loads are used to determine the efficiency of the corrugated waveguide system and Vlasov antennas. In the vacuum vessel radiation monitors determine the absorption by the plasma.

articleTitle: Precision measurement of mixer noise temperature and conversion loss
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Introduction Noise temperature measurements are fundamental to the development of low noise heterodyne mixers. Mixer noise and IF amplifier noise contribute to the overall system noise through the relation

articleTitle: Heterodyne detection at 10.6 um using quasi-planar metal-oxide-metal tunnel diodes
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Novel high performance symmetrical metal-oxide-metal tunnel diodes (MOMTD's) in a quasi-planar configuration have been successfully fabricated and, for the first time, used as room temperature detectors for the heterodyne mixing of two CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> lasers operating on the P14 line near λ = 10.6 um. Using these devices, we have achieved state-of-the-art NEP in the 4–6 × 10∼<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> W/Hz and a D∗ above 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> cm Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2/W</sup>. The junction area of these devices is in the 1–2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−10</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the junction oxide thickness is in the 12–15 A range (which is derived from the device's metals by reactive plasma process), the junction potential barrier lies in the 0.4 to 0.6 ev, and the series resistance is in the 5–10 Ω range. These MOMTD's were fabricated on thermal SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> grown on silicon substrates. These devices are batch processed fabricated using a fully plasma dry etch technology. Using this technology made it possible to realize high performance, high reproducibility, high yield, and high reliability as well as the fabrication of cluster type detectors having n × m detector arrays ranging from 10 × 10 to 700 × 1000.

articleTitle: Complex and backward-wave modes in finlines
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Complex and backward-wave modes, which are known in circular and rectangular waveguides with dielectric inserts, are shown to exist also in finlines. The effects of different finline parameters on these modes are studied. The nature as well as the dispersion characteristics are also investigated.

articleTitle: Determination of the broadening coefficient of 10 μ CO2 vi-rotation lines at different temperature
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The temperature dependence of the absorption coefficients of the vi-rotational lines in the IR spectra of carbon dioxide has been measured. The present work might serve as a basis for calculating theoretically the broadening coefficients, since the temperature dependent factor of the gas has been obtained.

articleTitle: Frequency tuning and bandwidth measurements for a high power 13CH3F laser
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A heterodyne receiver system has been developed for measuring the frequency spectrum of individual pulses from a high power optically pumped <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F laser. Results obtained thus far are for superradiant emission from the 245 and 248 GHz lines. The pump is a single mode TEA CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser, tunable ±800 MHz about line center. The superradiant emissions are found to consist of two or more individual frequency components, each is of narrow bandwidth (10–20 MHz FWHM). These components are found to remain fixed as the pump laser is tuned.

articleTitle: Far-infrared Cerenkov lasers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A 100 μm wavelength Cerenkov laser experiment has been planned. The device will be driven by a 5 MeV, 2 A (peak] microtron accelerator and the resonator will be a thin-film-loaded planar structure. Summaries of the theoretically-expected device performance and experimental progress will be presented.

articleTitle: A high repetition rate compact 94 GHz free electron laser
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The motivation for this work is to operate a practical free electron laser (FEL). The total volume of this device, including the accelerator and its modulator, is only 5 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The maximum duty cycle is 0.2% and the predicted peak power is 10 kW. The electron beam accelerator is a simple standing-wave RF-linac driven by a 5 MW. 1.3 GHz magnetron. The linac will accelerate electrons to an energy of up to 2 HeV at a micropul se current of 100 A with an average macropul se current, I, of 1 A. The initial two experiments will be an FEL amplifier and an FEL oscillator at 94 GHz.

articleTitle: Low noise submillimeter mixers in single mode waveguide
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Quasi-optical mixers using the cube corner geometry have demonstrated low noise performance over very wide bandwidths throughout the submillimeter, [1] but suffer from some significant disadvantages relative to millimeter wave mixers in waveguide. One of the most important is a rather poor beam pattern. Measured patterns of typical cube corner mixers at 692 GHz show a fairly symmetric main lobe but a large number of side lobes at the −10 dB level. This leads to a coupling efficiency to a typical single mode source of <50%, meaning that the effective receiver noise in a typical application is twice that measured with hot and cold loads. This low coupling also leads to a large local oscillator power requirement since the LO must be coupled in optically. In addition the typical mounting impedance for a mixer diode is fairly high and is not readily adjusted. This requires diodes of the lowest possible capacitance to obtain good performance. Waveguide mounted mixers can overcome all of these obstacles, but must use the minimum length of waveguide to avoid high input loss. In this work two such mixers have been built, one for 330–500 GHz and the other for 600–750 GHz, both designed for cryogenic operation. While the waveguides are very small, a simplified design and new assembly techniques make these practical devices to build.

articleTitle: Design of low noise millimeter-wave mixers taking into account the sources of excess noise in the diode
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Measurements show that the excess noise created in the Schottky diode by hot electrons and interval-ley scattering is important in millimeter-wave mixers. It is shown how this noise changes the diode optimum operating point and circuit impedances for best mixer noise performance.

articleTitle: Remote transmission of detected infrared signal by a pyroelectric detector-modulator
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Pyroelectric detectors have been used for remote sensing of temperature, thermal imaging and many other similar applications. However at longer distances between the source and the detector, many factors limit the detection sensitivity. It is therefore preferred to modulate the detected infrared signal so that it may be transmitted remotely and analysed.

articleTitle: Infrared and optical properties of windows
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Spectra of many different window glasses have been determined between 0.2 μm and 45 μm. They are discussed in relation to in-situ measurements on windows on a test cabin concerning temperature distributions, infrared and visible radiation, air flow and heat transfer.

articleTitle: Dither-free stabilization of CO2 lasers for far infrared pumping: A photoacoustic approach
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A method based on the photoacoustic technique is described for dither-free frequency stabilization of the optical pump in a CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH laser operating at 119 μm. Heterodyne measurements on two independently locked FIR lasers indicate excellent long term frequency and power stability. This stabilization scheme should be applicable to all optically pumped FIR lasants.

articleTitle: On the design of open resonators for quasi-optical gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In the design of a 120 GHz 200 kW gyrotron, we have analyzed the influence of the open resonator geometry on the electronic efficiency, the ohmic losses, the output coupling and the starting current. The method we have used to optimize the resonator design will be presented. The mode selectivity is improved by using a resonator formed by two mirrors with a central step.

articleTitle: The axial injection TEM orbitron maser
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We have completed the linear theory of the TEM orbitron maser which models the interaction of axially injected electrons orbiting the positively charged center conductor of a coaxial waveguide with the TEM waveguide mode. The theory treats electrons with arbitrary values of angular momentum. We will present the threshold values of the cavity Q multiplied by the electron beam power required for self-oscillation in a finite length oscillator configuration as well as the spacial growth rate calculated for an infinite length TEM orbitron amplifier.

articleTitle: Progress in quasi-optical transistor power amplifiers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Progress in the construction of a millimeter-wave power amplifier using an array of field-effect transistors and a novel quasi-optical power combining technique is reported. Experimental results from microwave models of the circuits are presented.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave imaging system with an endfire receptor array
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A millimeter wave imaging system, based on a 5×5 endfire (CWSA) receptor array, is described, which uses a 30 cm f/D=1 paraboloid. Resolution of two incoherent point sources at the Rayleigh distance has been demonstrated, and optical transfer functions have been derived. Preliminary work on integrated mixer elements suitable for this array is also described.

articleTitle: New theoretical thrusts in millimeter wave research
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Several new theoretical thrusts in millimeter wave research have emerged recently. At the Naval Research Laboratory and at the University of Maryland, work has been done on the analysis of the effect of complex orbits on radiation produced by a low density electron beam. Also work has been done on the effect of strong A.C. self fields for magnetized electrons with nearly circular orbits.

articleTitle: Far-infrared filter radiometry of stratospheric trace gases
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Recent advances in spectral knowledge and instrumentation may enable global mapping of the concentration profiles of trace gases by means of far-IR filter radiometry. We describe the design and radiative modeling for the measurement of OH rotational emission in the 100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> region.

articleTitle: Measurements of the absorption coefficient of various liquids at a wavelength of 0.119 mm
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Measurements were taken of the transmission of 0.119 mm radiation through 22 liquids using a variable length absorption cell for the preparation of the design of an acousto-optic modulator. Seven of these liquids were then selected to be tested at wavelengths of 0.185 mm, 0.307 mm, and 0.447 mm. It was found that a light grade of mineral oil proved to have excellent transmission in the far-infrared (FIR) spectrum. We were able, from the data collected, to estimate the index of refraction of these liquids at wavelengths longer than 0.3 mm.

articleTitle: A TE1,3 gyrotron at 85 GHz
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,3</inf> gyrotron to operate at 85 GHz with an output power of 300 kW has been designed, fabricated and tested. The device is described and results of the experimentation are given. A comparison to theory is made. Operation at the design frequency was achieved, and preliminary estimates indicate that output powers approaching 300 kW with efficiencies of 43% have been obtained.

articleTitle: Very high efficiency frequency tripiers for 100–300 GHz
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Varactor diodes are now available with very high cutoff frequencies suitable for application in mm-wave frequency multipliers. The theory of such frequency multipliers developed by Penfield and Rafuse [1] predicts comparable efficiency for doublers and tripiers, which for available diodes is >50% at 100 GHz. While doublers now approach this ideal when circuit losses are taken into account [2], tripiers have fallen well short of this goal. In this work computer studies have been made to predict the optimum embedding impedances for a mm-wave tripler, and model measurements have accompanied these in order to achieve optimum impedances In an actual unit. This work has resulted in a significant Improvement in tripler efficiency although results are still short of the theory.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave dielectric properties of single crystal strontium barium niobate (Sr0.61Ba0.39Nb2O6) at cryogenic temperatures
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The dielectric properties of single crystal SBN were measured for a number of samples at 30–50 GHz and at 90–100 GHz. Because of the recent availability of large high quality crystal samples from the ferroelectric materials development effort at the Science Center, we were able to make the first determination of the nonlinear coefficients dn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/dE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and dn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>/dE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> at liquid nitrogen temperature. The results are extremely encouraging, as it was demonstrated that these coefficients did not substantially decrease in value at low temperatures. In addition, the data provided the basis for a model to describe the fundamental mechanism controlling the susceptibility in this class of material.

articleTitle: Microlenses for a fly's eye imaging array
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The potential use of microlenses for imaging at millimeter-wave frequencies is investigated by analyzing the focussing properties of dielectric spheres. Our calculations show that the spheres of dielectric constant 12, with a quarter-wave matching layer, exhibit good focussing properties down to a radius of about one free-space wavelength.

articleTitle: High sensitive heterodyne IR laser interferometer
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In the recent measurements of plasma density by laser interferometer in large fusion machines/1/2//3/, a He-Ne laser is often used coaxially with IR or FIR lasers to measure the effect of the mechanical vibrations and subtract it from the observed fringe shift of the longer wavelength laser interferometer.

articleTitle: Linear polarization of the spectral thermal emission of IRON-cobalt alloys
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The perpendicular spectral thermal emission from iron-cobalt alloys with the magnetization parallel to their surface is partially linearly polarized. Measurements on this new even magneto-optic effect as a function of wavelength and temperature are discussed for several alloys.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band gyrotron experiment using an intense relativistic electron beam
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A new K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>-band gyrotron experiment is underway, using an electron beam from a compact Febetron puiser. Operating at 350 keV with a 700 A electron beam, the gyrotron has produced 20 MW (±3 dB) at ∼8.5 % efficiency at 35 GHz in a TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">62</inf> mode.

articleTitle: Electrostatic noise amplification in gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Electrostatic noise generated by the electrostatic cyclotron instability is analyzed and simulated in slab geometry with dc space charge effect neglected. The noise is found to be characterized by a broad spectrum, low saturation levels, and a strong disturbing effect on the electron energy distribution.

articleTitle: Slow wave monolithic variable phase shifter
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Monolithic technology development in the microwave and millimeter wave frequency regimes has put a burden on the device and circuit designers to increase component compatibility with solid state processing methods, including reduction of real estate area utilized, decreased cost per device, and increased yield. The phase shifter is no exception to this trend. Presently, several elements like GaAs MESFET's, lumped capacitors and inductors, diodes, and different electrical length (and impedance) transmission lines are used to realize phase shifters with between 3 through 5 bit capability, each bit being, for example, 22.5° or 45°. Depending upon the frequency region of operation, the number of elements, or their sizes, may present unacceptable levels of complexity or excessive use of GaAs real estate area.

articleTitle: Design considerations for high-gain SIS mixers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: It has been shown both theoretically [1] and experimentally [2,3] that the very sharp nonlinearity in the conductance of superconducting tunnel junctions can be used to implement millimeter wavelength mixers having high gain and very low noise, leading to the possibility of receivers that achieve the quantum noise limit. The junctions involved contain a thin insulating barrier between two superconductors, and are thus known as superconductor-insulator-superconductor (SIS) junctions. They are physically identical to Josephson junctions, but in this application the conductance is via the tunneling of quasiparticles (unpaired electrons), and so the Josephson effect is not involved.

articleTitle: Pulsed 140 GHz fourier transform microwave spectrometer
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An improved pulsed microwave spectrometer for the detection of rotational transitions in gaseous molecules in the frequency range of 130–150 GHz is described. It incorporates a tunable Fabry-Perot cavity and a low noise superheterodyne receiver for the detection of the molecular emission signals. The molecules are excited by π/2 pulses provided by a high efficiency frequency doubler which is pulse modulated at an IF frequency of 1.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Atmospheric effects on propagation
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The potential benefits to be derived from the use of radiation at frequencies near 300GHz for ranging and imaging have been apparent for many years but, in part because of nonavailability of convenient sources and detectors, until recently little quantitative research on the effects of the atmosphere upon such radiation has been conducted outside the Soviet Union. In the last few years, however, as potentially compact sources and viable detectors have come closer to realization the need for such quantitative research has become apparent. This paper describes a research program the objective of which is to both theoretically model and experimentally measure the effects of atmospheric turbulence and turbidity on waves at frequencies near 300GHz.

articleTitle: Polarmetric phase imaging for plasma current profile measurement
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Detailed knowledge of the structure of the poloidal magnetic field in tokamak plasmas is essential to an understanding of the startup phase, disruptions and general tokamak confinement problems. A non-perturbing technique for obtaining a measure of the magnetic field is via Faraday rotation of the polarization of a probe beam. The choice of probing wavelength is a compromise between maximizing the expected Faraday rotation angle (αλ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) whilst minimizing refractive bending due to plasma density gradients (αλ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and elliptization of probe, beam due to plasma birefringence (Voight effect αλ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>). The far infrared region of the spectrum is most useful in this application, though for most tokamak plasmas, maximum rotation angles are ≳20° so that some care must be taken to ensure an accurate measurement is obtained.

articleTitle: Study of density profile dynamics in the tokamak fusion test reactor (TFTR)
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A double pass multichannel far-infrared interferometer (Λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> = 119 μm) has been employed to measure electron density profile on the Tokamak Fusion Test Reactor (TFTR). This system provided valuable density information during a variety of plasma experiments. Density profile evolution during an adiabatic compression experiment was obtained and compared with TVTS results. Anomalous edge density behavior in “Marfe” discharges was observed. Also, density profile variation during solid pellet injection experiments has revealed several interesting features, such as peaked and hollow profiles.

articleTitle: Saturation of cyclotron maser instability driven by an electron loss-cone distribution
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The resonance diffusion of electrons in velocity space caused by the excited EM wave fields is considered to be the dominant saturation process of cyclotron maser instability that is driven by an electron loss-cone distribution. An upper-bound of the saturation level is derived analytically.

articleTitle: InP millimeter-wave Gunn sources
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Significant improvements in InP Gunn diode performance and manufacturing yields have been demonstrated with tighter controls over epitaxial growth and improved device processing. New InP source developments are being done with planar circuits at 35 and 94 GHz and with monolithic circuits at 35 GHz. Current limiting InP Gunn diodes are proving to be reliable designs operating over standard military operating temperatures and are also showing good room temperature operating life times.

articleTitle: Development of V-band integrated circuit frequency upconverters
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance of a V-band (50–75 GHz) single sideband upconverter using GaAs beam lead Schottky barrier diodes. An output power of 0.8 to 1.2 dBm has been measured with the carrier fixed at 57 GHz, and the modulating signal swept from 3 to 7 GHz.

articleTitle: Line competition and line selection in off-resonantly pumped systems
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: For some time already it has been known that off-resonantly pumped far infrared (FIR) lasers oscillate on the Raman line [1]. This feature has led to important applications such as the realisation of widely tunable CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F lasers (150–1200 μm) [2]. Only recently it has been shown [3] that mode competition is responsible for the fact that Raman oscillation (R) dominates line centre oscillation (LC) in a three-level system. The same considerations are valid in the equivalent situation of a single refilling transition (|0 > → |1> in Fig. 1). In certain experiments [4–7] Λ and V transitions (Fig. 1) appear in combination. For this case LC and R oscillations have been observed to exist simultaneously in one of the FIR transitions [5].

articleTitle: Absolute measurements of power in millimetre-wave and submillimetre-wave beams using photo-acoustic detection
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The paper will describe the design and operation of an absolute power meter for millimetre and sub-millimetre waves. The meter accepts a free-space beam up to 50 mm in diameter. It has a noise equivalent power better than 2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup> WHz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/2</sup>, and an absolute precision better than a few percent for signals greater than 10 μW.

articleTitle: An improved quasi-optical schottky-diode detector
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Experimental results of a novel quasi-optical Schottky-diode detector are reported. By use of a conical antenna together with the well-known whisker-corner-reflector antenna, a considerable improvement in the coupling efficiency between the diode and a laser beam has been achieved.

articleTitle: Studies of moist air properties up to 1 THz
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A millimeter-wave propagation model was developed that describes atmospheric medium properties. Experimental, analytical and theoretical details are presented as they pertain to formulation and validation of the model. An improved water vapor continuum was obtained from laboratory measurements of water vapor and moist air attenuation rates at 138 GHz.

articleTitle: New FIR CW laser lines in CH3OD and CD3OD optically pumped by a CO2 laser
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: More than seventy new lines have been obtained by using a waveguide FIR resonator in CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OD and CD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OD pumped by a low-pressure CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser emitting in the 9.4–10.4 μm classical bands and in the 10.8 μm hot band. The wavelength ranges were 46 μm-1.65 mm in CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OD and 60 μm- 1 mm in CD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OD.

articleTitle: The phase-correcting zone-plate
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A description is given of the use of the zone plate as a focusing or a frequency-filter device at millimeter wavelengths. Sample design data are given, as well as references to prior results. A newer type of zone plate is discussed which employs two dielectrics of equal thickness to produce a flat or planar zone plate.

articleTitle: DC design of mm-wave impatts on desk top computer
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In the development of mm-wave Impatts, the process of optimisation of doping profile which constitutes a major part of the design effort can be simplified to a great extent if de I-V characteristics are used to estimate the dc to rf conversion efficiency<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>. Having arrived at few such structure, the r.f. analysis<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,3</sup> can be carried out in detail using large signal simulation programmes to optimise the device-circuit interactions for final use. Therefore the availability of a fast algorithm of calculating dc I-V characteristics of Impatts is nighty desirable for design purpose in this context.

articleTitle: Reflection coefficients of oversized coupling holes
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The resonator of an FIR waveguide laser is constituted with a cavity loaded at each end with coupling holes. An input hole makes the pump IR beam enter and a larger output hole permits the FIR power beam to be generated /1/.

articleTitle: Mounting improvements of the MOM point contact diode
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A planar mounting structure is devised that renders the etched tungsten whisker and the nickel post one integral mechanical structure with possible orders of magnitude improvement in the mechanical stability of the hooked-tip MOM point contact diode. Experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Measurement of magnetic field direction by laser scattering with elliptical beam cross sections
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A pulsed hybrid CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser is used to measure the magnetised ion feature by collective scattering from a magnetically confined hydrogen arc. The necessary high angular and spatial resolution is achieved by a scattering geometry with elliptical beam cross section. The azimuthal magnetic field was obtained by scanning across the diameter of the current carrying plasma.

articleTitle: Far-infrared solar images observed from a balloon-borne platform
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Far-infrared brightness-temperature maps of the solar disk measured with a balloon-borne 60 cm diameter telescope at 40 km height on April 30, 1983 (active sun) and September 28, 1984 (inactive sun) are reviewed, compared and discussed with respect to present theories on the solar atmosphere.

articleTitle: Modelling and experimental design of a high gain free electron maser operating in the 30–50GHz range
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The conceptual design of a Free Electron Maser amplifier operating at 30–50GHz will be presented. The device, to be built at TRW during 1986, will operate in an extremely high gain regime. The models predict output powers in the 300KW range with the possibility of wide tunability (60%) and large bandwidth (10%). The design makes use of moderate system parameters (electron beam current ≃ 10A, energy ≃ 400kV, emittance ≃ 50π mm mrad) and beam prebunching to guarantee operation on the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode.

articleTitle: Stark CH3OH laser for phase locking with point-contact josephson mixer
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The point-contact Josephson junction mixer (J-J mixer) has been successfully used to detect beat signals between CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH FIR laser lines and 50 GHz microwave frequencies. To connect these frequencies directly by the phase locking technique, the Stark effect was applied to the CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH laser.

articleTitle: Intracavyty stark spectroscopy in optically pumped Fir lasers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Intracavity laser Stark-shift spectroscopy has been extensively used in. the past years as a practical and powerful tool for overcoming the limited tunability of the cw CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser. The extension o-f the method to the -far infrared (FIR) region has been demonstrated by using electric discharge HCN laser [1] with an extracavity absorption cell. The use of the optically pumped FIR laser is not straightforward due to the presence in the FIR laser of both the FIR and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pump fields. In fact high transmission Brewster windows in the FIR region can be made only by thin plastic films that are burned by the strong CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pumping field. In the laser magnetic resonance experiments the problem was solved by using a specially designed FIR laser cavity with an off axis optical pumping[2]. In the present paper we will describe a very simple method for performing intracavity Stark spectroscopy in optically pumped FIR laser by using as a FIR resonator a hybrid waveguide (HW).
