The HW is rectangular in cross section with two large metal walls and two short walls in a dielectric material. The E.M. field is transmitted with a low absorption only when is linearly polarized with the electric field parallel to the metal walls of the HW. As a consequence molecular transitions are induced only with the selection rule ΔM=±1 when a DC electric field is applied to the metal walls [3]. For this reason HW optically pumped FIR laser has been used for frequency tuning several FIR laser lines by Stark effect [3]. However in many laser lines the Stark effect is negligible and the output power and the frequency are not affected by the Stark field. It has been also demonstrated that a second molecular species can be introduced in the FIR cavity without a significant effect on the output power [4]. As a consequence it should be possible to perform an intracavity laser Stark spectroscopy in the FIR region by using a HW FIR laser emitting on a laser line unaffected by the Stark field and introducing also in the cavity the molecular species to be investigated. A decrease in the laser output power will be observed whenever a Stark component of this molecule is brought in resonance with FIR laser line. The frequency of many FIR laser line has been measured directly and the reproducibility has been found to be of the order of a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup> [5]. As a consequence the laser-Stark spectroscopy will provide a high resolution and very precise spectroscopic data in this region.

articleTitle: A method for measurement of Q-factor at millimeter wavelength
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The resonant frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and the quality factor Q are the fundamental parameters of microwave resonant system. In the microwave measurements, we usually use wavemeter to measuring resonant frequency f and both frequencies f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> of half-power points on resonant curve to obtain the figure of merit of resonant cavity: Q=f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>/f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. This method is simple, but in order to ensure measurement precision it is required that Q-value of the wavemeter is one order of magnitude higher than that of measured cavity. At mm wavelengths, the Q-value of cylindrical cavity resonator is rather low. It may be not able to measure Q-value of resonator that has above 1∗10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Multi-layered GaAs-AlGaAs millimeter wave impatt devices
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Studies of millimeter-wave IMPATT devices have demonstrated a drastic fall off of conversion efficiencies above 100 GHz. The saturation of ionization rates at very high electric field and the impossibility of maintaining the avalanche zone in a confined geometry are certainly two of the main fundamental causes of this degradation of performances [1].

articleTitle: A new noncontacting sliding short for millimeter wave applications
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A new type of a waveguide noncontacting sliding short is presented. The new sliding short consists of a waveguide-to-groove guide transition bifurcated by a sliding conductive partition of minimal thickness, oriented parallel to the propagating electric field. The simple structure is particularly attractive for millimeter-wave waveguide components, such as waveguide oscillators, mixers and detectors. Design details are presented for a sliding short prototype in G-band (140–220 GHz), which is incorporated in a subharmonically pumped balanced mixer.

articleTitle: CW optically pumped FIR laser lime from D2O18
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Optically pumped FIR laser lines have been obtained from about one hundred different molecular species with absorption lines coincident with the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> or N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O laser frequencies. The number of available FIR laser lines and the conversion efficiency change dramatically with the molecular species. CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH and CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are well known and especially rich of FIR laser lines below 200 μm.

articleTitle: The operation of a multicavity high-harmonic gyro-klystron amplifier
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The high-harmonic gyro-klystron relies on the synchronous interaction between axis-encircling electrons and a high order azimuthal TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n11</inf> cylindrical cavity mode. Harmonic operation together with RF acceleration of the electron beam constitute a compact moderate- to high-power millimeter wave amplifier. Experimental results for a fifth harmonic, four-cavity device are compared to theoretical predictions which assess gain, bandwidth, sensitivity to longitudinal velocity spread, self-oscillation and saturation characteristics. A gain of 37 dB has been achieved at the fifth harmonic of the cyclotron frequency. The peak output power was 65 W.

articleTitle: A 137 GHz gyrotron scattering diagnostic for instability studies in a tandem mirror
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A 1 kW, 137 GHz Gyrotron and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</inf> to TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode converters have been built and tested for a plasma scattering diagnostic on the TARA tandem mirror. The heterodyne receiver for this diagnostic has been installed. Plasma emission levels corresponding to a noise temperature of up to 173 eV double side band have been measured during ECRH in the TARA plug.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional simulation of the Ubitron/FEL amplifier
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The efficiency of the Ubitron/FEL amplifier is calculated from a three-dimensional nonlinear analysis and particle simulation code. Calculations show high efficiency and large bandwidths for the case of a monoenergetic beam with zero emittance. The efficiency falls off rapidly with increase in beam emittance. For high efficiency the spread in axial beam velocity should be less than 0.2%. Enhancement of efficiency by tapering the amplitude of the wiggler field is also discussed.

articleTitle: A dual frequency 183/380 GHz receiver for airborne applications
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A sensitive, dual-frequency millimeter-wave Dicke radiometer has been developed for use aboard the Kuiper Airborne Observatory. Using this receiver on the KAO observations were made of the 3<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</inf>→2<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> and 4<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf>→3<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> transitions of water vapor at 183.3 and 380.2 GHz in Orion and on Venus. The instrument uses quasi-optical techniques for beam guidance and injection of local oscillators and has cryogenically-cooled GaAs Schottky mixers. Calibration is by ambient and LN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-cooled aperture loads. The receiver can be used in either a beam-switched or load-switched mode. The SSB system temperature is 600 K and 1800 K for the 183 and 380 GHz channels, respectively.

articleTitle: Compact, high power, single mode fir NH3 laser pumped by a single mode CO2 laser pulse
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Temporally smooth and reproducible single mode NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> laser with 20 KW peak power (∼5 mJ energy) was obtained from a compact FIR laser cavity (0.5 m long) placed in the pump CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser cavity. A central dip was found in the pump CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser pulse, which was interpreted in term of Raman-like two-photon absorption.

articleTitle: A magnetron injection gun for the mit megawatt gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A magnetron injection electron gun has been designed and is under construction for use on a 140 GHz, 1 MW gyrotron oscillator operating in the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15,2,1</inf> mode. An 80 kV, 35 A beam has been achieved with a magnetic compression ratio of 30, a perpendicular to parallel velocity ratio of 2, and a low perpendicular velocity spread of 4%. Single parameter variations have been performed to determine the behavior of the gun.

articleTitle: CW-IMPATT's made from silicon molecular beam epitaxy material
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Silicon Molecular Beam Epitaxy (Si-MBE) offers several essential improvements when fabricating IM-PATT diodes whose active layer lengths are in the submicrometer region and whose doping profiles must be adjusted precisely. Both is supposed to be necessary for an efficient operation of W-band diodes.

articleTitle: A comparative analysis of chen and ulrich theories of meshes
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Metal meshes are important in the FIR region as beam splitters, as partial mirrors in Fabry-Perot interferometers and as component in hybrid couplers for optically pumped FIR lasers. These output couplers consist of a silicon or crystal quartz substrate, a dielectric coating for IR reflection and a metallic mesh for FIR reflection. The above list of mesh applications is largely incomplete.

articleTitle: The high power gyro-peniotron oscillator
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Start osoillation and non-linear optimized effioienoy are investigated for the gyro-peniotron oscillator. We consider here the TE(211) mode in a cylindrical cavity interacting with an axis centered electron team. The gyro-penlotron osoillator shows great promise for extremely high effioienoies, much greater than those obtainable through the cyclotron maser instability. In order to achieve these high effioienoies mode competition must be avoided, and an electron beam with a small guiding center spread must be used.

articleTitle: Analysis of the harmonic gyrotron travelling wave amplifier
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A single nonlinear differential equation is derived for describing the spatial evolution of the wave field in a gyrotron amplifier of the cylindrical guide geometry. This equation is then used to determine the efficiencies and the optimized interaction lengths for gyrotrons operated with TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N1</inf> modes at the N-th cyclotron harmonic.

articleTitle: Development of high power far-infrared lasers for fusion plasma diagnostics
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: There is currently considerable world wide interest in the study of high temperature plasmas. This interest is primarily driven by the goal of achieving controlled thermonuclear fusion which involves the release of net nuclear energy from the fusion of light nuclei such as deuterium and trituim. The far-infrared spectral region has proved particularly suitable in diagnosing the state of such plasmas. For example, the passive study of electron cyclotron emission from plasmas provides information on electron temperature. In addition, active probing using far-infrared radiation sources permits the determination of electron density via interferometry and the study of wave activity via collective scattering.

articleTitle: Avalanche photomultiplication in the far infrared
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We identify a process of avalanche photo-multiplication in arsenic-doped germanium initiated by far infrared (FIR) radiation at λ = 100–500 μm. The sample is biased above breakdown in a region of S-shaped negative differential conductivity (SNDC), so that electrons populate both the conduction band and excited states of donors. Primary photoionization then alters the dynamic equilibrium between impact ionization of donors and recombination leading to photomuliplication by a factor M> 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. A new FIR detector is thus provided with NEP ∼ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−12</sup>W(Hz)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/2</sup> and response time τ ∼ 1 ns.

articleTitle: High power Ka-band Goldstone solar system radar transmitter: Transmission line component development
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The Jet Propulsion Laboratory has initiated a design and development program for the next generation Ka-Band (34.5 GHz) 400 KW CW Goldstone solar system radar transmitter. The new transmitter will be used for radar observations of the near planets and asteroids. The radar signal is essentially a CW signal with a duration of approximately the round trip light time to the body under observation, which may range from 20 seconds to a few hours. The power amplifier to be used in the transmitter, a gyroklystron, is under development at Varian Associates in Palo Alto, CA. (1), and will not be discussed further in this paper. The transmitter will be housed on the 64 meter Cassegrain antenna at Goldstone, California. A transmission line will transport the microwave power from the gyroklystron to the antenna focus. This system must maintain mode purity, monitor certain characteristics of the signal, and provide efficient illumination of the subreflector. The remainder of this paper will describe the specifications for the transmission line components and theoretical and experimental results for several prototype components. The effects of mode purity on antenna performance will also be summarized.

articleTitle: Continuously tunable, split-cavity gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: GYROTRON III is the latest in a series of gyrotrons that have been built and tested at the University of Sydney (Brand et al. 1982, 1983 and 1984a, Brand 1985) in a program to develop tunable, broadband sources of milliraeter-submillimeter radiation with useful power levels. With a fixed cavity installed, this gyrotron can be tuned in steps over the 100 – 330 GHz frequency range simply be raising the magnetic field. It can provide watts of cw power.

articleTitle: Predicted performance at saturation of a high power CW gyroklystron amplifier using numerical simulation
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The behavior of a CW gyroklystron amplifier operating in the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">111</inf>/TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">121</inf> mode at saturation is examined using both a time-dependent electromagnetic particle simulation code and a steady-state, self-consistent field model. Multivalued solutions obtained from the steady-state code are shown to be a manifestation of the hysteresis-like behavior in the predicted drive curve obtained by using the time-dependent code.

articleTitle: Fluctuations in millimeter wave signals
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Since 1983, Georgia Tech, NOAA and the U.S. Army Atmospheric Sciences Laboratory have been engaged in a program whose purpose is to measure fluctuations in millimeter wave signals due to atmospheric turbulence, precipitation and fog [1,2]. Five measurement sessions have been conducted that have sampled atmospheric conditions in a variety of seasons. Frequencies of particular interest for their potential uses in higher precision imaging systems have been studied; namely, 116, 118, 142, 173 and 230GHz. These span a range of situations including windows between lines and regions near line centers. The measurements have been made over a 1.4 km path at a site near Urbana, Illinois, chosen for its exceptional flatness. It is important that the path and surrounding terrain be flat, homogeneous, and free of trees or other obstructions, so that the turbulence will not be perturbed by such irregularities. During this series of experiments, rigorous meteorological measurements have also been obtained.

articleTitle: The electronstatic electron cyclotron resonance maser
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A new kind of instability, the electrostatic electron cyclotron resonance maser(EECRM), has been presented and studied in this paper. The EECRM may have some attractive advantages, such as: it may be electronic tunable, it requires no magnetostatic field and it may operate at high harmonic and high mode.

articleTitle: Narrow band, temperature compensated dielectric filters for integrated circuits for the 140 GHz “Window”
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Low loss, high permittivity dielectrics offer the highest Q of the resonators that may be used with integrated circuits. At 140 GHz the small dimensions of the resonators suggest the use of certain low order mode resonators which offer bigger structures and higher Q's than the fundamental mode resonators. A band pass filter with a bandwidth of 1% is described. The effect of aspect ratio on computed mode resonances and the effect of substrate materials is also discussed.

articleTitle: Infrared faraday rotation of thin film In2O3+SnO2 semiconductors
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Two sets of thin film sputtered In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>+SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> samples, one prepared in argon atmosphere with oxigen and the other without, at various temperatures between 100 C and 250°C, have been studied by measuring their Faraday rotation from optical to infrared frequencies as well as their optical transmission spectra. The effect of the different treatments on the carrier densities and mobilities, show values that grow with the deposition temperature. This is seemingly due to an increase in the number of oxygen vacancies. On the other, hand, the presence of O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in the atmosphere during deposition, leads to smaller values, at the same temperatures, compared to those obtained in samples prepared in atmosphere without oxygen.

articleTitle: Observation of mode conversion in gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: At the University of Sydney three gyrotrons have been built and tested in a program to develop tunable millimeter-submillimeter wave cw sources of moderate power. GYROTRON III, the latest, can provide more than 10 W of microwave power over the frequency range 75 to 330 GHz. In order to keep the operating currents and the power levels low, the cavity is weakly coupled to the output waveguide by means of a short length of cutoff waveguide (Fig. 1).

articleTitle: Electron cyclotron emission measurements on TFTR
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The size of the latest generation of tokamaks (TFTR, JET, JT-60) relative to the smaller tokamaks leads to a number of advantages for the measurement of electron temperature using ECE. The longer period of the temperature sawtooth (typically 10–80 ms) in TFTR has allowed the study of profile evolution during a sawtooth. The higher values of the single-pass optical depth, resulting from the larger major radius, have allowed the temperature to be measured during plasma startup and near the plama edge, where the density and temperature are low. Furthermore, the spatial resolution relative to the plasma diameter has improved, making the detailed study of profile shapes possible.

articleTitle: Synchronous absolute calibration technique for in-situ calibration of the TFTR scanning millimeter wave radiometers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A synchronous signal averaging technique for calibrating the three Tokamak Fusion Test Reactor (TFTR) radiometers while they operate in the frequency scanning mode, between 75–220 GHz, will be presented. Improvements in accuracy and data collection efficiency will be discussed.

articleTitle: Cusptron microwave tube
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A cusptron microwave tube is operated at high harmonics of the electron cyclotron frequency. An axis rotating electron beam of 17 keV produces radiation at the sixth and twelfth harmonics with the six and twelve vane circuits, respectively. In the sixth harmonic case, the grazing condition is obtained at 250 G, and 0.5 – 1.0 kW radiation is produced at 4.36 GHz. In the twelfth harmonic case, it is operated in a tunable range of 7.4–8.2 GHz with 210 – 220 G, without the grazing condition satisfied.

articleTitle: A novel device for multimode analysis in oversized waveguides
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An instrument is presented which allows mode analysis of microwaves in oversized waveguides by measuring the spectrum of axial wave numbers. This wavenumber spectrometer consists of a leaky—wave antenna structure in the wall of the waveguide and of a movable receiver antenna with high directivity. From the radiation pattern of the leaky-wave antenna, as measured by the receiver antenna, the spectrum of the modes propagating in the waveguide is deduced.

articleTitle: System performance in rain in a radome-enclosed environment
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: As mentioned by Hogg and Chu (ref. 5), it is known that rain will influence the performance of microwave communication systems. The rain effects on a ground-based radome are of concern, and many studies on the prediction of a water film thickness (ref. 1) and experiemental investigations on the transmission loss of a wet radome with non-hydro-phobic and hydrophobic materials have been investigated (refs. 2,3,4,5). These studies show that the variation in water film thickness versus elevation angle in a wet radome may cause additional electromagnetic degradations, especially in the mm wave range.

articleTitle: Nonlinear analysis of MM wave tubes with soliton theory
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The nonlinear dispersion relation of mm wave tubes such as gyro-TWT, gyro-peniotron, etc. have been derived by using the kinetic theory of turbulent plasma. The nonlinear analysis has been worked out in terms of the soliton theory. The saturation energy density E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</inf>, phase shift Φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>, gain Φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</inf> and efficiency η are given as functions of system parameters.

articleTitle: Study on the FIR bandpass filters consisting op two resonant grids
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A series of FIR bandpass filters which consist of two resonant grids with resonant wavelengths λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> < 200μm were constructed. The dependence of the spectral characteristics of the filters on the separation between grids was studied experimentally in the separation range of 0 to 80 μm by means of the FIR Fourier transform spectrometer in the wavenumber region of 40 to 200 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, one of which is shown in Fig.(a). It is found that the resonant wavelength and bandwidth of the filter vary with the separation between grids, and the rejection in the stop-band is greatly increased and the maximum transmission coefficient in the pass-band is as high as 75%.

articleTitle: The analytic nonlinear theory of electron cyclotron maser
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Tremedous progress has been made in both theory and practice of gyrotron. However, most theoretical work done in the past contributes to linear theory with nonlinear theory only developed by computer simulation. In oder to understand the nonlinear interaction between electron and field more deeply it seems that the analytic nonlinear theory is necessary.

articleTitle: Flexible MM-wave dielectric waveguides
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Flexible dielectric waveguides have been demonstrated at 10 GHz and 94 GHz by filling hollow, low-dielectric-constant polymer tubes with low-loss, high-dielectric-constant powders. Flexible guides with losses as low as 0.12 dB/cm were demonstrated at 94 GHz. These guides also exhibited negligible bending loss for radii of curvature greater than 4 cm.

articleTitle: Polarization converters in overmoded circular waveguide for electron cyclotron heating (ech) at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Elliptic deformation of circular waveguide can produce arbitrary elliptical polarization from a linearly polarized TE11 or TM11 mode, used as intermédiates between TE01 and HE11 in ECH experiments. Measurements of a TM11 polarization converter for use on PLT are presented.

articleTitle: Design of a high-resolution FIR interferometer for the advanced toroidal facility at Oak Ridge national laboratory
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A 15-channel interferometer is being designed for the ATF experiment at ORNL. The interferometer will utilize a fan-beam geometry with an array of Schottky diode detectors. To minimize plasma refractive effects, an operating wavelength of 0.119 mm has been chosen. Details of the optics system design will be presented.

articleTitle: IR- and FIR- laser detection using antenna-coupled schottky diode
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Since the detection of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser using Schottky diodes was reported bv Tsang etal[1], the determination of optimum design conditions have attracted considerable attention.

articleTitle: Quasi-optical circuit design and applications
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Millimetre-wave quasi-optical systems (i.e. systems in which signal beams propagate unguided between lenses or mirrors under diffraction-controlled conditions because the widths of the beams are not several orders of magnitude greater than the wavelength) are being used in astronomy, radiometry, communications and the characterisation of materials. Compared with wave-guided systems, the quasi-optical approach offers high throughput and wide instantaneous bandwidth. It brings a penalty of larger size but careful design can give surprisingly small sizes without loss of efficiency.

articleTitle: A study of field and current distributions in finlines calculated with the spectral domain technique
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The effect of the number of spectral terms on the computing accuracy of finline characteristics is investigated extensively. The distribution of fields, currents, and the corresponding wave characteristics, are shown for several gap widths and numbers of spectral terms.

articleTitle: The inverse smith-purcell effect by using a sobmillimeter wave laser
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The inverse Smith-Purcell effect is one of the candidates for laser-driven linacs. The experimental apparatus to demonstrate the effect by using a sub-millimeter wave laser has been completed and will be described in this paper.

articleTitle: Full-wave analysis of suspended and inverted microstrip lines
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Suspended and inverted microstrip lines are one of the most commonly used planar transmission structures. They are especially suitable for the lower portion of the millimeter-wave band. At present, most of the available data on these lines is quasistatic. In this work, a full-wave spectral-domain analysis of the lines has been carried out. At millimeter-wave frequencies, the full-wave results display significant departure from the quasistatic values.

articleTitle: Far-field measurement technique for gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The far-field method to identify TE modes in a mixture radiated by an open-ended oversized cylindrical waveguide is extended to include an arbitrary angular position of the individual modes. The measurement technique using four antenna mapping system is presented.

articleTitle: Improvement of responsivity of 10.6μm hot carrier detector by resonant effect
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: It has been known that μ-type photo-conductive effect can be used to obtain sensitive detectors in far-infrared radiation regions[1]. Recently, μ-type photo-conductive effect due to the inter-valence band transition of germanium was observed at room temperature[2]. The characteristics on the detected voltage of the diode using this effect have been discussed at 10.6 μm band[3].

articleTitle: Computer-aided design of finline filters in waveguides below cutoff
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper describes a new design of optimized ladder-shaped finline filters in waveguide sections operating below cutoff. While the realization of conventional dielectric resonator filters requires precision machining of individual resonator blocks which must be mechanically adjusted in the reduced size waveguide section, the new design can be manufactured very accurately with photolithographic techniques, and the dimensions are optimally adjusted in a single design procedure. A rigorous field theoretical calculation of the individual waveguide discontinuities includes the interaction of higher-order modes and provides an accurate prediction of the practical filter response.

articleTitle: Analysis of coupling between two parallel dielectric waveguides
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The coupling between two parallel dielectric waveguides with a finite coupling length is investigated. The ends of the waveguides are tapered in order to reduce the scattering losses. It is shown that the taper sections can be utilized to achieve an effective coupling which is insensitive to the coupling length, thus, providing a much greater tolerance for the design and manufacturing of coupling devices.

articleTitle: Free electron lasers with spiraling electrons
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Experiments, theory, and computer simulations will be discussed concerning the generation of coherent millimeter wavelength radiation by spiraling electrons subjected to periodic wiggler magnetic fields.

articleTitle: Comparison between circular and conventional free electron lasers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We analyze the characteristics of a Free-Electron Laser (circular FEL) with a rotating electron beam in a uniform axial magnetic field and in azimuthal wiggler field, both in the low gain regime and the high gain regime, and compare with a conventional linear FEL. For a cold electron beam, the growth rate and efficiency of the circular FEL are higher than those of a conventional FEL, by a factor γ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</sup>, for fixed frequency. However, the circular FEL performance is more sensitive to the energy spread than the linear FEL. We also examine the influence of the negative mass instability on the circular FEL.

articleTitle: Kinetic theory of traveling wave gyro-peniotron
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Recently, there is more and more interest in gyro-peniotron because of its attractive advantages to gyrotron [1–4]. For example, gyro-peniotron has higher efficiency and more powerful RF output.

articleTitle: Analysis and measurements of a quasi-optical slot ring mixer
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A quasi-optical slot ring mixer is analyzed using a mixer analysis program and comparison is made between the predicted and experimental results. Applicability to the design of millimeter-wave slot ring mixers is discussed.

articleTitle: Some questions on the output signal-to-noise ratio of pyroelectric detector-amplifier systems
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The configurations of the coupling network which can effectively decrease the effect of the noise sources within the amplifier upon the equivalent input noise of the whole system are studied. The effect of feedbacks on the noise properties of the basic amplifier is analyzed and the quantitative results are derived.

articleTitle: Design of a submillimeter ellipsometer for the measurement of complex indices of refraction of materials
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The principle objective of the research is the design and fabrication of an automated submillimeter ellipsometer. The ellipsometer has been designed to measure the amplitude and phase of submillimeter radiation reflected from or transmitted through materials. The key component of the ellipsometer is a birefringent quartz plate which has an adjustable incidence angle. Control of this angle, as predicted by multiple reflection theory for birefringent dielectric plates<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, allows the retarder to be precisely oriented to produce a quarter wave retardation without the use of AR coatings. The radiation source is provided by CW optically pumped submillimeter laser lines, and a liquid He-cooled bolometer is utilized as the detector. Results of dielectric constant data measured with the ellipsometer will be reported.

articleTitle: Mo mirror produced by electron beam melting method for high power tea CO2 laser
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: High purity Mo mirror was produced by electron beam melting method and then the laser induced damage was studied for TEA CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser. It had a damage threshold 2 to 4 times higher than that of a Au coated glass mirror and had a life time 3 times larger than that of a sintered Mo mirror when the laser energy density higher than 60 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was irradiated. These good properties seem to be due to the surface with few voids.

articleTitle: Frequency measurememt of optically pumped FIR molecular lasers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Optically pumped far infrared molecular lasers play an important role in atomic and molecular. spectroscopy. Their frequency reproducibility is of the order of few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup> and the emitted power can be easily of few milliwatts. At frequency higher than ITHz, sources of comparable spectral purity and power are not available. Wavelength measurements are limited to a maximum relative accuracy of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> – 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup>, while the maximum accuracy can be reached only by direct frequency measurements. Nearly BOO frequency measured laser are available at present (1).

articleTitle: Observation of high-power millimeter wave emission from a virtual cathode
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Intense bursts of mm wave power have been observed in microwave generation experiments with a relativistic electron beam (REB) virtual cathode oscillator.(1) In this device an electron beam is injected into a drift space at a current above the space-charge-limit, and a potential develops downstream which is large enough to reflect electrons back to the source region. Two mechanisms can give rise to microwave oscillations in a virtual cathode device: electrons reflexing between the real and virtual cathodes, and oscillations in the amplitude and position of the virtual cathode. Typically both mechanisms are present, but in the present experiments reflexing has been shown to be dominant.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization of millimeter wave sources
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: As the use of the millimeter wave (MMW) bands increases, the need for better spectral control of sources also increases because of widening application of this spectrum to Doppler radar, communication, and measurement systems. As the millimeter bands become more crowded, better frequency control will become necessary to avoid interference. There is also a real advantage to be gained in source power stability by phase-locking; locked sources typically exhibit output power stabilities of a few tenths of one percent. Phase locking of MMW sources to a frequency standard also provides the basis for frequency measurements which are perhaps the most accurate measurements of any physical quantity ever made, with accuracies of 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−12</sup> being attainable. Phase-Lock circuits using both linear and digital techniques are available to the MMW system designer, and both types are discussed in this paper along with some typical results obtained.

articleTitle: Planar dipole-fed mixer arrays for imaging at millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The excellent sensitivity of single planar mixers at 140 GHz (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf> = 4900K DSB) has led us to investigate arrays of mixers, each fed by planar dipole antennas. Model measurements of impedances and mutual coupling, as well as fabrication and tests at millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths, are described.

articleTitle: Real time infrared image processing
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The paper studies the techniques of real time infrared image processing. The enhancement of real time infrared image is mainly discussed. With enhancement of real time infrared image, the authors suggest main methods that are local histogram equalization, pseudo color display, average of multiple frames and accumulation of multiple fields, contour enhancement and restoration coefficient. Emphasis is laid on the restoration coefficient method, in this paper. On the basis of describing the model of the method, the concrete project for realizing enhancement of the real time infrared image is put forward, and the practical example is given.

articleTitle: The optimum pumping power for optically pumped FIR lasers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The relations between the output power of optically pumped FIR laser and the pumping power were studied theoretically by solving the density matrix equation of four level system by means of the matrix signal flow graph method. The output power density of FIR laser was. calculated by the iterative method. A set of curves of output FIR laser power density against pumping power has been obtained. It has found that every such curve has a maximum point of which the position is different for different pumping detuning. According to these results we predicted that there would exist an optimum power density for an optically pumped FIR laser with certain pumping detuning. This theoretical result would help us to design the optically pumped FIR lasers.

articleTitle: Parameter Studies for a 150 GHz Gyrotron at KfK
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Of several methods proposed to enhance the efficiency of a gyrotron, contouring the wave electric field profile (by contouring the cavity cross section) [1] and contouring the applied DC magnetic field [2] are among the most promising. In the present study we consider both methods in combination. Thus, we compute numerically the efficiency as a function of applied magnetic field (magnitude and tapering), beam parameters (initial kinetic energy, guiding center radius, and α=v⊤/v‖), maximum HF field strength and resonator geometry. Our model is applicable to whispering gallery modes as well as azimuthally symmetric ones. The aim of this study is twofold: to understand the dependence of the efficiency on the various parameters and to use this information to select one or more suitable design parameter sets for the KfK experimental gyrotron program. The selection criteria include not only maximum efficiency at high output power but also starting current, startup behavior, ohmic losses and sensitivity to mode competition.

articleTitle: Electron trajectories in the free-electron laser with a uniform magnetic field and a corrugated slow-wave structure
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An iterative method is described for evaluating electron trajectories due to forces coming from a corrugated slow-wave structure and a uniform magnetic field. The objective of these evaluations is to characterize the free-electron laser capable of generating radiation in the far-infrared/microwave spectral region.

articleTitle: Power combining of solid state millimeter wave sources
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Very efficient power combining of solid-state millimeter wave sources may be obtained through the application of quasi-optical resonators and monolithic source arrays. Through the theory of reiterative wave-beams (beam modes) with application of the Lorentz recipocity theorem it is shown that planar source arrays containing 25 individual elements or more results in very efficient power transfer of energy from the source arrays to the fundamenmtal wave-beam mode. It is further shown that for identical sources within a properly designed quasi-optical power combiner the output power tends to increase much faster that number of source elements.

articleTitle: High resolution millimeter-wave imaging sensor
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A scanning, dual polarization, 3-mm radiometer has been built for use on a small aircraft to produce real-time high angular resolution (0.5°) images of the ground during atmospheric conditions (smoke, dust, and clouds) in which IR and visual sensors are not usable. The preliminary mm-wave images from the first test flights and analysis will be presented.

articleTitle: Win frequency fir sources for plasma diagnostic applications
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The FIR spectral region is particularly well suited to diagnose the state of fusion plasmas. For example. FIR interferometers and polarimeters are used to infer electron density and plasma current profiles via phase and polarization modification of a probe beam. In addition collective scattering techniques in the FIR have been used to probe a variety of turbulent and coherent waves that exist in these plasmas. The density fluctuations associated with these waves may be responsible for the observed anomalous transport in fusion devices.

articleTitle: FAR infrared spectroscopy of superconducting NB3GE films
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Ge, with its high T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> of 23K has been examined by tunneling. but far infrared spectroscopy has been used only in the normal state.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> Here we present the first far infrared transmission and reflection measurements near the gap on thin Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Ge films below T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>. One main result is the observation that like other high-T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> materials (e.g. V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Si and NbN) which lie between the extreme dirty and extreme anomalous limits. Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Ge's optical properties require a finite scattering time for their description. A second is that the data can be explained only by the assumption of a layer of normal or low-Tc material between the top superconducting layer and the substrate. This result, shows how far infrared radiation, penetrating the entire film, gives information not available from tunneling experiments, which probe only a coherence length.

articleTitle: Design and cold testing of a high peak power X-band gyroklystron
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The main goal of the University of Maryland's gyroklystron project is to develop an efficient, high power, high gain, phase controllable amplifier at 10 GHz. While peak powers of several hundred megawatts are ultimately of interest, our initial experimental design values include 30 MW of output power in 1 μs pulses with a gain in excess of 50 dB. The 30 MW power level represents an enhancement of almost three orders of magnitude over the current state-of-the-art in gyroklystron amplifiers.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,2</sup> This enhancement will be achieved by going to high beam energies (γ ≈ 2) and overmoded cavities TE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>. Outlined in this report are the steps being taken to realize our goal.

articleTitle: A new “twin-beam” mig for high power gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: With the development of the gyrotron towards higher power and shorter wavelength, the key part of the gyrotron, the magnetron injection gun (MIG), has been studied. Here, we present a new structure of MIG double-beam gun as shown in Fig(1).

articleTitle: Cosmic-ray noise in bolometers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Penetrating charged components of cosmic-rays produce noise spikes in sensitive infrared detectors. The problem is illustrated by recent experimental data obtained at balloon altitudes of ∼40 km, and similar effects occur at all altitudes. The overall nature of cosmic-ray noise will be reviewed so that this everpresent and highly non-Gaussian noise background can be minimized appropriately in the design of high sensitivity bolometers and their associated data acquisition systems

articleTitle: Watt-level monolithic quasi-optical diode frequency multiplier grid
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: At millimeter wavelengths, harmonic frequency multipliers are widely used to produce local oscillator power for heterodyne receivers; however, the output power level is limited to only a few milliwatts due to the fact that only a single varactor element is employed. Recently, Archer demonstrated a dual-diode. doubler with an output power of 26mW at 105 GHz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1)</sup>. However many applications such as imaging arrays require considerably more power. To satisfy this need we propose a monolithic quasi-optical diode grid design for high power harmonic frequency multiplication.

articleTitle: Calibration of the FIR polarimeter on TFTR tokamak
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The results of the first Faraday rotation measurement on the TFTR tokamak are presented. Data are reported on ohmic-as well as neutral-beam-heated plasmas including solid pellet injections. The procedure and the results of the calibration are described. The effects of various errors in the measurements as well as the problem of cross coupling laser beams are studied.

articleTitle: Thermal filamentation instability of millimeter waves in laboratory plasmas
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: During the electron cyclotron resonant heating of laboratory plasmas by intense millimeter waves, the thermal filamentation instability can be excited to cause significant fluctuations in plasma density and magnetic field. These pump wave-induced perturbations may affect the plasma confinement.

articleTitle: EPR in dysprosium aluminium garnet at FIR wavelengths
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Using an optically pumped FIR-laser, the EPR-spectrum of DAG is studied as function of frequency and temperature, with the magnetic field (up to 7.5 Tesla) parallel to the [001] and [111] directions. Several resonances are observed and tentatively explained.

articleTitle: The efficiency of electron cyclotron masers with longitudinal wiggler
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: It has been investigated theoretically<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> that a relativistic electron beam with finite transverse dc momentum passing through a region of combined uniform solenoidal and longitudinal wiggler magnetic fields is capable of generating coherent radiation at frequency Ω≈2γ where w<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> and V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> are respectively the electron cyclotron frequency and electron axial velocity, but the energy conversion mechanism is concluded to be a low efficiency process. The output frequency is uneable and is higher than either a free electron laser with the same wiggler wave number or a Doppler-shift dominated cyclotron maser with the same solenoidal field. On the other hand, it has been shown through computer simulations<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> that a Doppler-shift dominated cyclotron maser can convert 25% of the beam kinetic energy into coherent radiation. In this paper we carry out computer simulations to demonstrate that using the magnetic configuration described above also has potential to achieve high efficiency.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave integrated circuit radar sensors
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The marriage of planar integrated circuit transceivers with thin, printed antennas is providing a new generation of low cost, producible and miniature millimeter wave transducers for demanding systems requirements. The use of integrated circuit techniques for millimeter wave transducers has now moved from a research curiosity to an engineering discipline. Microstrip is the preferred transmission media to demonstrate a wide variety of RF component functions. For applications involving precision weapon systems, a soft substrate is preferred since it provides lower cost, improved survivability, and functional versatility when compared with the traditional hard candidates such as quartz. The MESFET is rapidly emerging as a key building block for monolithic supercomponents up to a frequency of approximately 40 GHz.

articleTitle: Developments in two dimensional arrays
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A two dimensional array of individual millimeter wave antennas with detectors will be described. The array is placed on a substrate lens [1] in the focal plane of a primary lens to form an imaging system (Fig. 1.). Calculations which predict ideal efficiencies of over 90% will be presented. Fabrication of the array and preliminary measurements will also be discussed.

articleTitle: Performance of heterodyne mixers using arrays of SIS junctions
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The SIS quasiparticle tunnel junction has been demonstrated to be the most sensitive mixing element for millimeter wave receivers [1,2]. Conversion gain greater than 1 and noise temperature approaching the quantum limit [3,4] has been observed. The required local oscillator power, which can be as small as 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup> W, leads to a low saturation threshold for these mixers [5,6]. The practical benefits, including higher saturation power, of using series arrays are sufficiently important that a substantial number of experiments using arrays have been reported [2,6,7,8,9]. It has not been clear, however, whether there has been any sacrifice in mixer conversion efficiency (gain) or noise. We present a systematic experimental investigation of mixing performance in series arrays of N junctions, where N = 1, 5, 10, 25 and 50.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave complex refractive index, complex dielectric permittivity and loss tangent measurements of common polar and non-polar polymers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We are presenting data for polyethylene, polypropylene, poly-4 methyl pentene-1 (TPX), polytetrafluorethylene, plexiglass, acrylic and nylon over the frequency range 50–300 GHz., The first four are non-polar and exhibit extremely low loss characteristic. The last three are typical polar polymers but exhibit nearly twenty to thirty times higher loss than polar-polymers.

articleTitle: The 8 to 14 μm window of the terrestrial atmosphere
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Continuum and line spectra of the terrestrial atmosphere in the 8 to 14 μm window are reviewed on the basis of in-situ measurements with airborne radiometers as well as with laser-photoacoustic spectroscopy in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Measurement and assignment of new fir laser lines in 12CH3OH and 13CH3OH
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We have found twelve new lines in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH and thirty three in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH. Both molecules are pumped by a regular cw CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser. Two of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH and ten of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH FIR laser lines are assignned to specific rotational energy levels in the excited C-O stretch state.

articleTitle: Design of cusptron amplifier for accelerator applications
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Research and development of an RF source for next generation electron-positron colliders is proposed based on the newly developed cusptron microwave tube. The intended parameters for prototype cusptron are 100 MW peak mcirowave power at 8.5 GHz using 240 MW beam. In order to reach this ultimate goal, first the scaling law of the beam and field parameters for the cusptron is examined, and the RF circuit design in conjuction with these beam parameters are presented. The design parameters for the scaled-down experiments, intended as intermediate steps and tests for the scaling laws, are also given.

articleTitle: Invited Keynote: Advances in millimeter-wave microstrip sources and amplifiers
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The past decade has seen increased applications for millimeter waves both in commercial and defense activities. Conventional millimeter-wave solid-state sources were built in waveguide, suspended stripline, and finline. Fabricating these components in microstrip provides advantages of light weight, small size, and low cost. This paper summarizes the recent developments in millimeter-wave microstrip solid-state sources and amplifiers.

articleTitle: Balanced monolithic mixer for use at 44 GHz
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Receiver front ends for satellite applications require low noise devices that have been space qualified to withstand shock and vibration during launch and to operate reliably for many years with continuous LO power and cyclic temperature changes as the satellite passes in and out of earth's shadow. Whisker-contacted Schottky barrier diodes that were hermetically sealed in copper-ceramic packages were developed for the Lincoln Experimental Satellites LES-8 and LES-9 [1], Pairs of these diodes were mounted in a two-diode balanced waveguide mixer. Although these diodes have operated flawlessly in space for over nine years, difficult and time-consuming manufacturing procedures were required to provide this level of reliability. This is because the device essentially used a mechanical pressure contact between an etched gold-plated tungsten whisker and a 3-μm diameter Schottky barrier metallization. As device diameters were reduced to submicrometer dimensions in order to provide low capacitance for operation into the submillimeter region, the difficulties of whisker contacting and reliability of the resulting contact under shock and vibration were of even greater concern.

articleTitle: Grazing-incidence FIR gas laser
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Detailed studies on performance and theory of the first grazing-incidence gas laser are reported. Its cavity is formed of a tuning mirror and exchangeable gratings with full- and half-wavelength periods. Also discussed is the phase-matching by a variable waveguide-matched discontinuity in the grating.

articleTitle: Absolute calibration of detectors for mm-submm radiometry
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Absolute millimeter and submillimeter radiometry, as used for example in plasma diagnostics, requires the absolute calibration of detectors over a wide spectral range and at good spectral resolution. Some of the special considerations which arise when designing equipment to do this will be examined.

articleTitle: Phase imaging systems for measurement of plasma density contours
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: During recent years, there has been considerable interest in obtaining spatially localized time resolved density measurements in fusion plasmas. However, the study of such phenomena requires many channels of information on a scale much finer than available with current discrete chordal view multichannel interferometers. These problems can be overcome by imaging an expanded probe beam occupying the entire plasma port crosssection onto a linear detector array<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>, thereby significantly reducing the number of optical components and hence the cost and complexity of the system compared with a comparable discrete chord multichannel interferometer. Other more fundamental advantages of the imaging technique include compensation for phase errors due to plasma refraction, whilst the diffraction limited system resolution (typically ≃ 1cm for FIR probe wavelengths) allows the use of many detector channels for high spatial sampling rates. and hence accurate reconstruction of the density profiles.

articleTitle: CO2 lidar system for pollution monitoring
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: At the ENEA Centre of Frascati an infrared LIDAR facility is being developed primarily for atmospheric studies. The TEA CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser head and other sub-systems are described in this paper.

articleTitle: New FIR laser lines in CD3OH
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In this communication we report laser action in CD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH optically pumped by a regular continuous wave CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser. We have made laser wavelength, optimum pressure of the gas, relative polarization and intensity measurements of 135 FIR laser lines, 69 of which observed by the first time.

articleTitle: Intracavity triple resonance in the CH3OH far infrared laser
publicationTitle: 1985 Tenth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A very interesting aspect of FIR laser spectroscopy is its contribution to the physical insight of the laser active molecules themselves. In fact, a molecule can display several FIR laser emissions only if its spectrum is dense and extended enough so as to have high coincidence probabilities with the available pump lines (usually CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). This usually means serious difficulties in the spectrum assignments, since experimental and computational inaccuracies lead to very frequent ambiguous cases. On the other hand, new line assignments are a continuous challenge to further improvements in the molecular model. The use of optical pumpimg for the excitation of the FIR lasers allows the direct application of external CW and oscillating fields to the active medium, thus making, for instance, Stark effect and triple resonance (IR-FIR-RF) experiments possible. The study of the Strak behavior of a FIR laser emission can give valuable hints for the J and K quantum numbers involved in the laser cycle [1]. Triple resonance experiments have proved to be very important for the study of the A symmetry states of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> OH [2, 3], the richest laser active molecule known up to now. Here RF transitions are induced between the components of K-splitting doublets involved in the laser cycle. According to the position of the doublet in the cycle, an RF resonance is detected as a power decrease (common upper level of the pump and laser transitions) or increase (lower level either of the pump or of the laser transition) in the FIR emission, see Fig. 1.
